introduce:
Stand with your thighs closed, and raise your hands over your head. 

Then bend your knees and come to a sitting position. 

Bend your torso forward slightly and extend your arms forward to keep your balance. Hold this position till time’s up.
name: CHAIR

tips.text: Please don’t let your knees go over your toes.
Please put your weight on your heels.
This exercise is beneficial to your arms, legs and cardiovascular system.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand on the floor with your feet together. 

Then bend your body and bring your upper body as close to your legs as you can. 

Hold this position for a few seconds and repeat.

Exhale when you bend your body and inhale when you come up. Keep your legs straight during the exercise.
name: FORWARD BEND

tips.text: Please keep your legs straight.
This exercise stretches your hamstrings.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands directly under your shoulders. \n\nStraighten your legs, and lift your hips up in an upside down \'V\' shape. Spread your feet apart, and spread your fingers. Transfer your weight back to your legs. Hold this position.
name: DOWNWARD FACING DOG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
If it\'s too hard for you, please bend your knees slightly.
Please keep your back straight.
Please sink your shoulders.
Please keep your arms tight.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Lay prone on the ground with your arms supporting your body. 

Bend your arms and lower your body until your upper arms are parallel to the floor. 

Keep your body straight. Hold this position.
name: PUSH UP HOLD

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your body straight.
Please tighten your core.
Breathe naturally.
Don't sink or raise your hips.

introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart. Draw your belly in and tuck your tailbone down. Roll your shoulders back and down. 

Bend your upper body forward and rest your hands on your legs. Bend from your hips instead of your waist. 

Focus on keeping your back flat and lengthening your spine. Hold this position.
name: HALF FORWARD BEND

tips.text: Bend from your hips instead of your waist.
Keep your legs straight but don\'t lock your knees.
Focus on keeping your back flat and lengthening your spine.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise stretches your hamstrings.
This exercise strengthens your back.

introduce:
Lay prone with your hands under your shoulders and the tops of your feet on the floor. 

Slightly lift your legs off the floor. Straighten your arms and open your chest toward the ceiling. 

Your gaze will go up slightly. Hold this position.
name: UPWARD FACING DOG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Rotate your shoulders back and down.
Keep your legs engaged, don\'t slouch them on the floor.
Keep your neck natural, don\'t strain your neck.
This exercise stretches your chest, abdomen, and spine.
This exercise can firm your buttocks and thighs.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-distance apart. Take your left foot forward while keeping your right leg straight.  

Turn your right foot 60 degrees to your right. Lower your body until your left thigh is almost parallel to the floor. 

Raise your arms toward the ceiling with your palms facing each other. 

Draw your belly in, tuck your tailbone down, and lift your chest. Hold this position.
name: WARRIOR I LEFT

tips.text: Keep your front knee facing forward.
Don\'t let your front knee go over your toes.
Keep your neck relaxed.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Keep your hips facing forward.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
This exercise strengthens your thighs, shoulders, and back.
This exercise stretches your chest, hips, and legs.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-distance apart. Take your right foot forward while keeping your left leg straight. 

Turn your left foot 60 degrees to your left. Lower your body until your right thigh is almost parallel to the floor. 

Raise your arms toward the ceiling with your palms facing each other. 

Draw your belly in, tuck your tailbone down, and lift your chest. Hold this position.
name: WARRIOR I RIGHT

tips.text: Keep your front knee facing forward.
Don't let your front knee go over your toes.
Keep your neck relaxed.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Keep your hips facing forward.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
This exercise strengthens your thighs, shoulders, and back.
This exercise stretches your chest, hips, and legs.
Breathe regularly.
